newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weak on ample supplies, Oman bearish.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weak on ample supplies, Oman bearish.

text.p: Activity on the Middle East crude market picked up drastically, with several cargoes of July Oman and Abu Dhabi crudes heard traded.
The main buyer was a U.S. major, who was heard buying at least three cargoes of Umm Shaif -- from a shosha and two European majors -- plus two partial cargoes of Oman.
But the increased demand failed to boost prices, with the Oman deals heard done in the range of MPM -22/24 cents per barrel, the deepest discounts yet for July.
Chinese buyers were not heard in the market, which led to the depressed Oman prices, traders said.
The Umm Shaif trades were all done on a Dubai-related basis, rather than on a differential to ADNOC prices.
Traders said sellers preferred to sell on Dubai linked prices rather than at steep discounts under ADNOC.
It was also hoped that the Dubai/ADNOC differential would narrow further for August liftings, ultimately equating the levels to a smaller discount to ADNOC prices.
The Umm Shaif deals were done around Dubai +75, which traders say is equivalent to around ADNOC -45.
A European major sold two parcels of Murban at Dubai +1.05, probably the last Murban barrels for July, traders said.
A major confirmed buying July Al-Shaheen at Dubai -30 early this week. But rumours Bangchak bought Al-Shaheen were not confirmed.
Ample supplies of June Minas were continuing to put pressure on prices. There were widespread rumours of a June parcel sold by a shosha to China at ICP -8, although the trade could not be confirmed.
With most June requirements already covered, and some shosha still holding June Minas, traders expected very aggressive offers to emerge. --Azlin Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3199)
